title: The SIF Reference Report (revised version)
contribution: Definitive reference for the Standard Input Format: an MPS-compatible, three-file format (SDIF/SEIF/SGIF) that encodes group partially separable structure (groups, element types, internal variables) of large nonlinear programs so that problems can be exchanged and codes compared validly.
problem_entry: Practical bottleneck: entering LANCELOT test problems with thousands of variables was time-consuming and error-prone, and recoding differences undermined valid comparisons between codes (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Structure = invariant subspaces, not sparsity; write functions as group functions of weighted sums of element functions on small variable subsets, with internal variables u = Wv and element/group types, as an MPS superset (pp. 4-7, 10).
assumptions: No mathematical assumptions; design constraints: structure mandatory, MPS compatibility (fixed format), OS independence, Fortran six-character names (p. 3).
proof_devices: none (format specification); only chain rule W^T grad_u f, W^T Hess_uu f W for elemental derivatives (p. 44)
positioning: De facto base is MPS; modelling languages (GAMS, AMPL, OMP) handle repetition but not invariant-subspace structure; factorable/functional-form proposals awaited (pp. 3, 61).
writing: Requirements listed as bullet considerations with honest costs ('not all of which are pleasant'); three worked examples before syntax; revision keeps early-1990s wording and a wrong section cross-reference (pp. 2-4, 61).
limits_future: Rigid fixed format, formidable for small problems, free form shifts responsibility to user; hopes for a true nonlinear modelling language (pp. 2-4, 60).

Make a new standard a strict superset of the de facto one and list the costs you accept (p. 3)
coauthors: N. I. M. Gould, D. Orban, Ph. L. Toint

quotes.text: These differences could be a major obstacle to valid comparisons between competing optimization codes.
The importance of invariant subspaces is that nonlinear information is not required for a function in this subspace.

title: Framework for large-scale modeling and simulation of electricity systems for planning, monitoring, and secure operations of next-generation electricity grids
contribution: A 16-author IBM white paper (DOE RFI response) surveying security-constrained unit commitment/economic dispatch, massive grid data processing and large-scale grid simulation, and setting a research agenda of parallel, decomposable, stochastic optimization with convergence guarantees.
problem_entry: Operator pain at real scale: aging, congested grid near transfer limits; commercial IP solvers handle about 100 units/24 periods/50 scenarios while real instances have thousands of buses and over 1000 generators (pp. 1, 3-4).
key_idea: Survey plus method-choice rules: hybrid computing for parallel scenarios and decomposition (p. 5); DFO only when no derivatives (about 200 variables serially), SA/GA/Nelder-Mead rarely best, no finite differences under noise, use AD (pp. 13-14, 46).
assumptions: No formal model; cautions that Benders/GBD on nonconvex AC problems lacks convergence or even local-minimizer guarantees (pp. 10, 19).
experiments: none (literature figures only, e.g. >10x speedup on 16 processors, p. 11)
positioning: Recommends Conn's own Trust-Region Methods, DFO book and LANCELOT next to IPOPT and ALGENCAN; criticises engineers' use of non-state-of-the-art methods (pp. 12-13, 19).
writing: Agenda framed by concrete scale counts and numbered challenge lists; explicit rules of thumb with thresholds; inconsistent treatment of AD (p. 13 vs p. 46); a mis-matched reference [87] (pp. 13, 62).
limits_future: Future: real-time UC/ED for thousands of generators, joint UC + AC-ED MINLP by decomposition, structured stochastic SCUC/SCED, convergent large-scale optimization, virtual power grid (pp. 15-19, 55-56); no own method or data.

title: On the local convergence of a derivative-free algorithm for least-squares minimization
contribution: Proves local quadratic convergence of the DFLS derivative-free least-squares algorithm for zero-residual problems under a local error bound (weaker than Jacobian nonsingularity) and shows in long-budget tests that DFLS beats NEWUOA and finite-difference LMDIF in accuracy and evaluations, with and without noise.
problem_entry: Completing an existing algorithm's theory: global convergence and small-budget numerics were in the SIOPT 2010 paper; this adds the local rate and high-accuracy numerics (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Show that, with base point = current iterate, DFLS eventually selects the regularized Hessian J^TJ + k||m||I, safeguards stop firing and the trust region becomes inactive, so DFLS becomes a regularized Levenberg-Marquardt-type method; then reuse Fan-Yuan's SVD local analysis (pp. 4, 9-20).
assumptions: Bounded level set; uniformly bounded model Hessians; zero residual with local error bound ||F(x)|| >= a dist(x,X*); base point eventually x_k; iterates assumed to converge to X* (pp. 7-9).
proof_devices: criticality step (Lambda-poised in radius proportional to ||g||) gives model-Jacobian error <= L3 dist(x_k,X*) (Lemma 3.1, p. 10)
error bound + Taylor show regularized branch eventually chosen, lambda_k proportional to ||F(x_k)|| (Lemma 3.2, pp. 10-12)
step bound ||d_k|| <= 2 dist(x_k,X*) by comparing with feasible point xbar_k - x_k (Lemma 3.3, pp. 12-13)
|r_k - 1| -> 0 and Delta_k bounded below, so trust region inactive (Lemma 3.4, pp. 13-16)
SVD split of model Jacobian (Fan-Yuan) for quadratic rate (Lemma 3.6, Thm 3.7, pp. 17-20)
experiments: DFLS vs LMDIF and NEWUOA, 10^5-evaluation cap, stringent stop; 25 zero-residual (HS equality problems recast + collected), 22 nonzero-residual, absolute and relative 1e-2 noise with 10 runs and solver resolution set to noise level; DFLS uses 1/5-1/10 of NEWUOA's evaluations on zero-residual problems (pp. 20-26).
positioning: Builds on CSV geometry/framework and Powell's NEWUOA; imports LM error-bound local theory (Tseng, Yamashita-Fukushima, Fan-Yuan); reconciles with the small-budget findings of the SIOPT paper (pp. 2, 9, 17, 26).
writing: Contribution stated in abstract's third sentence; constants tabulated up front; proofs detailed but one lemma delegated to [8]; hedges the small test set explicitly (pp. 1, 3, 18, 22).
limits_future: Zero residual only, subclass only, convergence to X* assumed, small partly ad hoc test set, O(mn^2) extra storage; future: convergence of bound-constrained DFBOLS (pp. 9, 21-22, 26).

title: Lagrangian relaxation based decomposition for well scheduling in shale-gas systems
contribution: A Lagrangian relaxation scheme for field-wide shut-in scheduling of shale-gas multi-well pads (GDP-derived MILP, one subproblem per pad, trust-region-stabilized cutting-plane dual, fix-and-local-branching primal heuristic), with frequency-weighted proxy-model tuning, that beats a same-time full-space MILP on all nine test sets.
problem_entry: Application: cyclic shut-ins remove liquid loading, but the single-pad MILP becomes prohibitive field-wide; weak coupling between pads suggests Lagrangian relaxation (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Dualize the single linking constraint on pad reference rates to decompose by pad; stabilize the cutting-plane dual with a 1-norm trust region and actual/predicted ratio test; recover primal feasibility by fixing binaries plus LP and local branching (pp. 16-20).
assumptions: Proxy valid only above critical rate; constant regional compressibilities; constant reference rate; Lagrangian feasible set a polytope by assumption; independent wellhead control makes exact tracking impossible (pp. 6-7, 12, 17, 25).
proof_devices: Lagrangian bound at least LP-relaxation tight (Geoffrion) (p. 16)
trust-region cutting-plane with serious/null steps and ratio-based radius update (Algorithm 1, pp. 18-19)
bound lambda >= -1 via LP duality and Fourier-Motzkin elimination (Appendix A, pp. 29-30)
a priori solution for lambda >= 0 seeded into the cutting-plane model (p. 19)
experiments: Nine sets (3/6/9 pads x 7/14/21 days, six wells per pad), GAMS+CPLEX 12.3, vs full-space MILP given about the same wall time: duality gap 0-22.9% vs 63.3-100%, better upper bound on all nine, dual in 4-9 iterations (pp. 20-24).
positioning: Builds on Whitson's cyclic shut-ins and own single-pad MILP/proxy papers; imports boxstep/trust-region stabilization, GDP hull/big-M reformulation, unit-commitment min-up/down inequalities and local branching (pp. 2, 12-20).
writing: Engineering-venue structure (model, tuning, formulation, algorithm, results, discussion); candid self-assessment ('only average' by gap) and long, specific future-work list (pp. 22, 25-26).
limits_future: Gaps above 10% on several sets, weaker for long horizons, nonconvex tuning, proxy mismatch for short shut-ins; future: augmented Lagrangian or branch-and-price, Lagrangian decomposition, per-well and temporal decomposition, parallelism, quadratic stabilization (pp. 12, 22, 25-27).

title: Solving aircraft conflicts by continuous optimization and mixed-integer nonlinear programming
contribution: Two-page abstract announcing a MINLP and a continuous exact-l1-penalty formulation for aircraft conflict avoidance by speed and heading changes, plus a separation-maximizing robust variant, solved by couenne (global) and ipopt (local).
problem_entry: ATM safety (5 NM separation) and controller workload call for automation; levers are both speed and heading (p. 1).
key_idea: Remove the infinite-dimensional separation constraint (Cafieri-Durand) and linearize angle terms; model logical separation either with binaries (MINLP) or with an exact l1 penalty (continuous) (p. 1).
experiments: Unquantified: 'a set of problem instances'; MINLP global via couenne, penalty model local via ipopt 'extremely rapidly'; separation-maximizing variant much faster (pp. 1-2).
writing: French-conference abstract, promissory ('will be presented at the conference'), adjectives instead of numbers (pp. 1-2).
limits_future: Aim: decision-aid tool for controllers about 20 minutes before conflicts; no limits stated; journal version S099 replaced the l1 penalty by the smooth quadrant penalty and dropped the robust variant (p. 2; S099 pp. 12-13).

method_links.note: exact-penalty lineage carried into ATM next to a global MINLP (thin, abstract only)
framed as a decision-aid tool for air-traffic controllers

transferable: Offer a robust variant that swaps a hard nonlinear deviation objective for a linear separation objective and report its speed separately (pp. 1-2)

quotes.text: where we introduce an exact l1-penalty function, tailored to the problem at hand, to deal with the difficult aircraft separation constraints.
The overall proposed optimization approach is expected to serve to design a decision-aid tool for air-traffic controllers to solve conflicts at the tactical level (i.e., 20 minutes before conflicts).

title: Mixed-integer nonlinear and continuous optimization formulations for aircraft conflict avoidance via heading and speed deviations
contribution: Two new models for aircraft conflict avoidance with speed and heading deviations (a trigonometry-free MINLP and a continuous quadrant-penalty NLP) and a three-phase local-then-global method that proves global optimality on 14 of 15 30-aircraft instances, including CP instances only locally solved before.
problem_entry: Separation is a feasibility problem made optimization by secondary criteria; literature uses speed or heading alone; the earlier continuous model (Peyronne-Conn et al.) was local and used finite differences (pp. 3-4).
key_idea: Change variables (q, theta) -> (q, omega, pi) so relative velocity is linear with one quadratic equality per aircraft; model the parabola-based logical separation by complementarity (MINLP) or smooth quadrant penalty (NLP); chain NLP-Penalty -> fixed-binary global solve -> full MINLP with cutoffs (pp. 5-20).
assumptions: Same flight level, straight lines, uniform motion, simultaneous maneuvers at t=0, initial separation, speed in [0.94,1.03]v, heading within +-pi/6, no altitude change or recovery (pp. 4-7).
proof_devices: strict convexity of f_ij reduces for-all-t separation to a logical condition on the parabola minimizer (p. 6)
four sign cases of known heading data give bilinear linking constraints and valid bounds (pp. 8-10)
feasibility (q=1, theta=0) and zero lower bound of NLP-Penalty (p. 14)
explicit caveat that the per-term leaning property of the penalty is lost in the nonseparable nonconvex sum (p. 14)
experiments: Literature CP/RCP instances from [17,26]; AMPL, COUENNE (600 s), IPOPT+MA57; MINLP global for CP up to 19 aircraft (<4 s) and all RCP 10/20, 7/15 RCP 30; NLP-Penalty zero penalty on all RCP; three-phase global on 14/15 RCP 30 (pp. 13-21).
positioning: Builds on Cafieri et al. parabola approach and the quadrant-penalty report [11]; claims instances unsolved by Rey-Hijazi and Dias et al.; criticises the earlier Peyronne-Conn-Mongeau-Delahaye continuous model (pp. 3-4, 16).
writing: Contributions paragraph with 'main' and 'second' contribution; remarks after each model; honest caveat on penalty non-separability before results; posthumous dedication (pp. 2, 4, 11, 14).
limits_future: Local infeasibility of the penalty model, one unsolved instance, simultaneous maneuvers only, no trajectory recovery; future: autonomous vehicles, non-simultaneous maneuvers, dynamic environment (pp. 4, 14, 20-21).
